classification.difficultyReason: Constructs interior and exterior distance loci, including quarter-circle arcs at the square's corners.

content.prompt: The vertices of a square are located at coordinates $(2,2)$, $(-2,2)$, $(2,-2)$ and $(-2,-2)$.

answer.worked: Plot the four vertices and join consecutive vertices around the perimeter. The sides lie on $x=\pm2$ and $y=\pm2$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Draw the set of points inside the square whose shortest distance from the perimeter of the square is one unit.

answer.short:
The boundary of the smaller square with vertices $(1,1)$, $(-1,1)$, $(-1,-1)$ and $(1,-1)$.

Each side is one unit inside the corresponding side of the original square.
answer.worked:
Inside the square, the shortest distance to its perimeter is the least perpendicular distance to its four sides. Move each side inward by one unit. The required locus is
$$\max(|x|,|y|)=1,$$
the square boundary with sides $x=\pm1$ and $y=\pm1$.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 12(b); teacher PDF page 66, printed page 441
spec.description: Original square in black and smaller concentric square locus in standard blue; unshaded, with source axis and corner-marker features.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Draw the set of points outside the square whose shortest distance from the perimeter of the square is one unit.

answer.short: An outer rounded-square boundary: four parallel segments one unit beyond the sides, joined by quarter-circles of radius $1$ centred at the four vertices.
answer.worked: Opposite each side, draw a parallel segment one unit outside the square: $y=\pm3$ for $-2\le x\le2$ and $x=\pm3$ for $-2\le y\le2$. Beyond each corner, the nearest point on the square is that vertex. Join adjacent segments with an outward quarter-circle of radius $1$ centred at the vertex.

spec.mathematics: Four offset segments at x=±3 or y=±3 and outward radius-1 quarter-circles centred at (±2,±2).
